newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says to name new finance minister June 20.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says to name new finance minister June 20.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Thursday he would name a new finance minister to replace Amnuay Viravan on Friday to oversee the troubled national economy.
He did not name any prospective candidates.

He also told a news conference that there would be no change in the current policy of defending the baht against speculative attacks and that finance and foreign exchange stability were his government's top priority.
"First, I will name an acting finance minister. And I will continue to monitor the finance ministry and will do so more closely as it is essential," he said.

"The important thing is that we will carry out measures that have been started, especially in the policy of fixing the baht where there will not be any change. And the new finance minister will continue this policy," he said.
Chavalit also appealed for more time to tackle Thailand's growing economic problems and said he would retain Amnuay's finance and economic policies.

"In order not to leave a long vacuum, we would try to wrap up our consideration (of a new finance minister) today. And tomorrow, we should be blessed with an auspicious occasion for an audience with the King for his appointment of a new finance minister," Chavalit said.
